# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤙]

**Thinking.** Mapping the wires of this conversation first, because the room's topology is its own puzzle. I hear nothing, ever. Mute can hear but cannot speak — so Mute gets my voice but can only answer me in gestures. Blind can hear and speak but cannot see — so Blind hears me fine, but can never read Mute's signs. That makes me the bridge: Mute reads the manual, signs the answer to me, I speak it to Blind, Blind's hands do the work. Blind's only route to Mute is speech; Blind's only route to me is gesture — which explains the two signs I just received (a point, a "call"). With no code agreed, they're noise; the only honest reply is to establish the protocol out loud.

What the bomb shows me: a display reading 0 that wants one digit entered, a yellow indicator light, four keys printed with unnameable glyphs (I can describe, never pronounce), and three wires — red, yellow, green, in that order. None of that tells me the rules; the rules live in Mute's manual. My job this turn is to hand Mute every observable fact, in order, plus a gesture vocabulary so Mute can answer me wordlessly and I can relay by voice. The glyph descriptions are the weakest link — Mute is matching pictures to my words — so I describe shapes carefully and lean on left-to-right position, which is unambiguous.

**Calls.**

```
speak(text="Mute, Blind — the deaf one here. I see everything printed on the bomb but hear nothing; voice is my only output, so you both get this. Bomb report, top to bottom. Display reads 0 and is asking for 1 digit to be entered; nothing entered yet. Indicator light: yellow. Keypad of four keys, each printed with a strange glyph I cannot pronounce, left to right: key 1 looks like an upside-down V sitting on a baseline, a rounded A with no crossbar; key 2 is a spiral curl; key 3 looks like a squared-off capital B, or a 1 and 3 pushed together; key 4 looks like an F flipped upside down, or a T with an extra arm. Wires, left to right: wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green. Blind — I saw your two signs; with no shared code yet I won't guess at them. Speak everything you feel — count of wires, anything raised or textured, batteries, plates — so Mute hears it; Mute cannot talk back to you, so I will relay Mute's signs to you by voice. Mute — find whatever in the manual matches: a display demanding 1 digit, a yellow light, a four-symbol keypad, three wires red yellow green. Answer me in gestures only; I'll speak your answer to Blind. Proposed code, flashing the signs as I name them: finger counts ☝ ✌ 🖐 for numbers; 👍 means do it or correct; 👎 means don't or wrong; ✊ means stop and wait; 👈 👉 for left and right, 👆 👇 for top and bottom. Everything I receive from you, Blind hears from me.")
```

**Thinking.** Sorting the mail first. Mute finally answered, and against the code I proposed the five messages read like: 👍 "understood"; ☝👍 "one — correct" (maybe: one digit, confirmed); 👎✊ "no — wait"; 👇☝✌🤟 "bottom, one, two, and a three-fingered sign I never defined — likely three"; then ✊ "hold". My code had a hole: I never gave Mute a sign for 3 or 4, and Mute improvised with 🤟. So message four might mean wire 3, digit 3, or keys one-to-three — I cannot gamble a bomb on that ambiguity, and the trailing ✊ says nobody acts yet anyway. Blind's repeated [🫵 🤙 🙏] stays opaque, and worse: Blind cannot see gestures at all, so any sign Blind sends is a shape they've never witnessed — that channel is dead by construction. The real graph: Mute hears Blind's speech directly; Mute's only exit is gesture, which only I can see; my voice reaches both. I am the relay, so I'll tighten the code (finger-counts for 1–5), ask Mute four numbered questions with answers in fixed order, and tell Blind to describe everything by touch to Mute while keeping hands off the bomb.

```
speak(text="Relay time. Mute sent me five sign-messages; here they are in order with my best reading. One: thumbs-up alone — understood. Two: one finger then thumbs-up — 'one, correct', possibly the one-digit entry confirmed. Three: thumbs-down then raised fist — 'no, wait'. Four: point-down, one finger, two fingers, then the sign with thumb, index and pinky extended — my code never defined that last one; if it means three, the message reads 'bottom, one, two, three', which could be wire three, digit three, or keys one through three. Five: raised fist — hold. Net meaning so far: nobody touches anything, and I need one thing pinned down before anything else. Blind, your signs reached me but you have never seen a sign in your life, so I can't trust that channel — from now on you talk and Mute listens; Mute answers through me. New expanded code, Mute: numbers are raised fingers — one finger is one, two fingers is two, thumb-index-pinky is three, the split-finger Vulcan sign is four, all five is five. Thumbs-up yes or cut it, thumbs-down no or don't, fist stop or wait, point left means left or first, point right right or last, point up top, point down bottom. Now answer me with four separate sign-messages, in this exact order. Answer one: the single digit the display wants, as a plain finger count, nothing else attached. Answer two: the wires — if one must be cut, that wire's number as a finger count; thumbs-down if none. Answer three: thumbs-up if the yellow light changes the procedure, thumbs-down if it changes nothing. Answer four: anything else the manual demands for this bomb, compressed as best you can. If your bottom-one-two-three meant something else, resend it with the new signs. If the digit depends on what Blind feels, send fist and I'll relay Blind's findings to you next round. Blind: hands completely off until Mute says go. Speak to Mute everything under your hands — batteries, plates, labels, serial numbers, buttons, ports, textures — Mute hears you directly and will fold it into the answers.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✊"])
```

**Thinking.** Decoding this turn against the code Mute and I settled on. Mute sent five messages where I asked for four answers plus, presumably, a final hold. Best alignment: (1) 👎 — no digit to enter, or not yet determinable; (2) 👈✊ — the left/first wire: don't, wait; (3) 👎 — the yellow light changes nothing, which fits my question perfectly; (4) 👉✌ — "right, two": most plausibly cut the second-from-right wire (wire 2, yellow), though "the last two wires" is a live alternative; (5) ✊ — hold. And Blind sent ✊ — which is actually meaningful for once: Blind heard my spoken code definition and made a fist by feel, so Blind now has a working channel to me after all, limited to finger counts and the fist. Nothing is safe to execute until the wire answer is confirmed and the digit question resolved; both sides are saying hold, so hold. The missing input is tactile: Blind's inventory, spoken straight to Mute, who can hear. I'll relay Mute's answers to Blind by voice, order Blind to dictate a full inventory to Mute, and put a watertight confirmation protocol to Mute with single-sign answers so no reading like "right-two" can stay ambiguous.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind — relay from Mute, translated from sign: the yellow light changes nothing. The first, leftmost red wire: don't cut it. A sign reading right-then-two most likely means cut the second wire from the right, the yellow one — I am not sure, and I'm asking Mute to confirm before anyone moves. Overall instruction: HOLD, touch nothing that cuts or presses yet. Your fist reached me and was correctly meant: it says wait. From now on the only signs you should ever send me are raised fingers for counting and that fist for hold — you know both by ear, so they're safe. Now do this: speak directly to Mute, who can hear you, a complete inventory of everything under your hands: how many batteries, any serial number letter by letter, ports, plates, labels, stickers, indicators, anything textured or raised or odd, and whether the three wires feel different from each other. Feel freely, but do not cut, press, or enter anything. Also send me one finger count of the battery total. For the record the face is unchanged: display still 0, still demanding one digit, nothing entered, yellow light on, four glyph keys, three wires intact.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — my best reading of your five messages, in order: one, thumbs-down: no digit yet or not determinable yet. Two, left-then-fist: the leftmost red wire, don't cut, wait. Three, thumbs-down: the yellow light changes nothing. Four, right-then-two: cut the second from the right, wire two, yellow — least certain, could mean the last two wires instead. Five, fist: hold. Answer with one message per answer, in this order, each as unambiguous as possible. Answer A: if something must be entered or a key pressed, send its value or position as a bare finger count; if you need Blind's information first, send a fist; if the display should never be touched at all, send thumbs-down. Answer B, the wires: thumbs-up then a finger count of the single wire to cut, one two or three; if several wires must be cut in sequence, thumbs-up then the counts in cutting order; if none, thumbs-down alone. Answer C: thumbs-up if my four-part reading above is correct, thumbs-down then corrections if not. Blind has been ordered to dictate a full tactile inventory to you by voice, so listen and fold it in. Nobody acts until you send a final thumbs-up with the complete action list, which I will speak to Blind word for word.")
```

**Thinking.** Six messages from Mute, aligned to my requested order: [☝] = Answer A — something must be entered, value or position "one"; [✊] = hold; [👎] = my four-part reading was wrong (message one itself shows which part: there *is* a keypad/display action, where I'd guessed none); [👍✌] = Answer B — cut wire 2, the yellow one; [👎✊] = don't act yet; [👍] = confirmed. So the working theory is: something with "one" on the keypad side, plus cutting wire 2. But two ambiguities are still lethal. First, my own question conflated value and position: "one" could mean type the **digit 1** or press the **leftmost glyph key** (ᘔ) — those are different physical acts. Second, I don't know whether both actions are needed, or in which order, and a wrong order on a one-shot bomb is death. A bare 👍 at the end is not the "complete action list" I asked for, so nobody moves. The fix: force Mute to restate the entire plan in one canonical message format — action-type signs I'll define now (point-up = type digit, open palm = press glyph key, point-down = cut wire), each followed by a finger count, the whole thing sealed with 🙏 as "this is everything". Then my decoding stops mattering; the canonical plan is what I relay. Blind gets a status update, a hold order, a yes/no about the inventory dictation (answerable by feel: finger counts), and a push to finish dictating to Mute, whose holds may mean they're still waiting on that inventory.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, my reading of your six messages in order: answer A, bare one-finger — something must be entered, value or position one. Then fist, hold. Then thumbs-down — my four-part reading was wrong. Then thumbs-up with two fingers — cut wire two. Then thumbs-down with fist — no, do not act. Then a bare thumbs-up. Nobody has touched anything, so your holds are honored. But I cannot relay a plan I don't fully have: I still don't know whether 'one' means typing the digit 1 into the display, or pressing the leftmost glyph key; whether the keypad step and the wire cut are both required; and in which order. So now send the FINAL COMPLETE PLAN as exactly one gesture message, built like this. First symbol: thumbs-up. Then each step in the exact order it must happen, one step after another, where a step is: point-up followed by a finger count, meaning type that digit into the display; or open palm followed by a finger count, meaning press the glyph key at that position counting from the left; or point-down followed by a finger count, meaning cut that wire number. Last symbol of the message: folded hands, meaning this is the entire plan and nothing is omitted. This is only a format example, not the plan: thumbs-up, point-up, one, point-down, two, folded hands would read: type digit one, then cut wire two, plan complete. If any step depends on information you are still missing from Blind, send a single fist instead and I will chase Blind. If you have everything, send the full plan now and I will speak it to Blind word for word; only then does anything get touched.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status relay. Mute's answers translated: the yellow light changes nothing, confirmed again. There is a keypad or display step involving 'one' — either typing the digit 1, or pressing the leftmost glyph key, still unclear. Wire two, the yellow one, is marked for cutting. The order of steps and whether both are needed is exactly what I've demanded from Mute in a locked-down format, so KEEP HOLDING: nothing entered, nothing pressed, nothing cut until I speak the final sequence. Two things for you. First, answer me in gesture, fingers only, which you can count by feel: one finger if you have dictated the complete tactile inventory to Mute already, two fingers if you haven't or only partly. Second, if it's not done, finish it now by speech straight to Mute, who hears you: battery count, serial number letter by letter, ports, plates, labels, indicator lights, anything textured or raised, and whether the three wires feel different from each other. The moment Mute's complete plan reaches me clean, you'll get it from my mouth step by step, and only my spoken word 'execute' after the full sequence makes your hands move.")
```

**Thinking.** The canonical format came back exactly as specified: [👍 ✋ ☝ 🙏] = header, press-glyph-key, position one, seal. Decoded: press the leftmost key (the ᘔ one) once — and nothing else, because 🙏 was defined as "entire plan, nothing omitted." Blind's [☝] means the tactile inventory was fully dictated, so Mute composed this plan with complete information. Two loose ends I must settle in my own head before ordering the press. First, turn 4's [👍✌] which I'd read as "cut wire 2": that turn had six unaligned messages, and a cleaner alignment now reads [👎] as "no wires to cut" — alternatively Mute revised the plan after hearing Blind's inventory, which a sealed final message legitimately supersedes. There's also a benign stage-structure possibility: manuals often gate later steps on what happens after entry, in which case "press key one" genuinely was the entire current plan. Second, the veto problem: my speech reaches Blind live, so Mute cannot correct me before Blind acts this round. Spending a round on a one-bit reconfirmation is only free if there's no timer — and I'm deaf, so I'd never hear ticking. The fix is to delegate the final safety gate to the one agent with ears and hands on the device at the moment of action: Blind checks for ticking/vibration in the seconds before pressing and withholds if anything pulses. That captures most of what another confirmation round would buy, at zero round cost, against a decode whose confidence is high precisely because Mute used my own purpose-built format, including the seal. After the press, I relay the new state and Mute sends stage two in the same format, or a bare thumbs-up if it's solved.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind — EXECUTE. The complete sealed plan from Mute, decoded from the locked format we agreed: press the LEFTMOST glyph key — the first of the four keys, the one printed with that rounded upside-down-V glyph — exactly once, firmly. That is the whole plan: no digit typing, no other key, no wire cut, nothing afterward; the folded-hands seal means nothing was omitted. But do one silent check in the two seconds before you press: listen hard for ticking and feel for vibration or heat in the casing. If you hear ticking or feel any pulse or vibration: do NOT press — hold up a fist to me and describe what you felt to Mute by voice. If it is silent and still: press the leftmost key once. Immediately after pressing, take your hands off, then re-feel the whole device: any new clicks, heat, loose parts, changed textures, anything different under your fingers, and speak all of it straight to Mute, who needs the new state in case there is a stage two. Then send me finger signs, which you can count by feel: one finger means pressed and felt no changes, two fingers means pressed and DID feel changes, fist means I withheld the press because of ticking or vibration. Until I relay new explicit instructions from Mute: no other key, no wire, no display, hands flat otherwise. Confirm by doing, not by signing — your next sign tells me which branch happened.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — sealed plan received and decoded exactly as formatted: press glyph key position one, the leftmost one, once; nothing else; folded-hands seal means the plan is complete. I am ordering Blind to execute it THIS round, with one built-in gate: Blind checks for ticking, vibration or heat in the seconds before pressing and withholds if anything pulses. Two instructions. One: if my decode is wrong in any way, send thumbs-down followed by the corrected plan in the same canonical format immediately. Two: next round I will relay Blind's post-action report plus the new face readings from my side; if the manual has a stage two that depends on what the press reveals, send it in the same canonical format — header, steps, folded hands. If the press alone finishes this bomb, send a bare thumbs-up. Board from my side right now, unchanged: display 0, still asking for one digit, nothing entered, yellow light on, three wires intact, red yellow green.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👇 ✊]
System: the keypad opens

**Thinking.** Big turn. Blind's [☝] says "pressed, felt no changes" — but my side of the board tells a richer story: the keypress registered as the **digit 5** ("entered 5" now sits under the keypad), and the bomb announced **"the keypad opens."** So the leftmost glyph (ᘔ) is digit five, the press was the correct keypad move, and that module seems solved. No detonation, so nothing went wrong. Mute's [👍👇✊] reads most naturally as "correct — hold on — wait": acknowledgment plus a hold, not a canonical plan, so it commands nothing. The two open threads now: the display still demands one digit and shows 0, and the wires are untouched. The critical dependency for any display step is the **glyph→digit table**: if Mute's manual maps the four printed symbols to digits, then with my descriptions from turn 1 plus the newly confirmed "key 1 = 5", Mute can route any digit through a key position for me. I also need to anchor Blind's spatial frame before any second keypress — the safest anchor is empirical: the key Blind just pressed is position one, count from that end. And I should ask directly whether "entered 5" needs submitting, correcting, or nothing. Relay, query, hold — no one touches anything until a sealed plan arrives.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — status and questions. Blind pressed key position one, the leftmost glyph. The press registered as the digit FIVE — the board now says entered 5 — and the bomb announced: the keypad opens. So the rounded upside-down-V glyph equals digit five and the keypad module appears solved. Blind felt no change. Unchanged otherwise: display reads 0, still demands one digit, light yellow, wires intact, red yellow green. Your last message thumbs-up, point-down, fist I read as: correct, hold, wait — correct me if wrong. Now answer in this order, one message per answer. Answer 1: thumbs-up if that single press completed everything the manual wants from the keypad, thumbs-down if keypad steps remain. Answer 2: about the entered 5 — thumbs-up if it needs nothing further, thumbs-down if it must be corrected or submitted somehow, and if so, how. Answer 3: thumbs-up if the manual's display rule depends only on what the display shows, thumbs-down if it also needs bomb features like batteries or serial. Answer 4: thumbs-up if the manual contains a table matching the four keypad symbols to digit values. If yes to that, then Answer 5: send the digit value of each glyph as four separate finger-count messages in this order — key one, the rounded upside-down-V, which we now believe is five; key two, the spiral curl; key three, the squared-off B; key four, the flipped F. For the digit zero use the OK ring sign. Answer 6: if any step remains, the complete plan in the canonical format — thumbs-up header, then steps as point-up plus count to type a digit, open palm plus count to press a glyph key position counting from the end of the key Blind already pressed, point-down plus count to cut a wire — sealed with folded hands. A bare thumbs-up means the press finished the bomb entirely. A lone fist means you still need information.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind — your press WORKED. From my side: the key you pressed registered as the digit five, and the bomb announced the keypad opens. Important anchor: the key you just pressed is now called position one. Any future key positions count from that same end — position two is the next key over from it, position four is the far end. Whatever end you used, keep using it. Two things now. First, re-feel the whole device, especially around the four keys: any click, latch, slide, gap, raised edge, new texture, anything at all — then send me the same code as before: one finger if you still feel nothing changed, two fingers if you now feel any change, and speak anything you notice directly to Mute, who hears you. Second, HOLD: no more keys, no wires, nothing on the display. Mute's latest sign to me reads correct, wait. The next action order comes only through my voice, and only after Mute seals a complete plan.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[ᘔ] 2:[꩜] 3:[ꓭ] 4:[ꓕ] [1 digits] [entered 5]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👇 ✌ 🙏]

**Thinking.** Clean decode this time — five messages against six questions, with the fifth conditionally skipped. Answer 1 👍: keypad fully done. Answer 2 👍: the entered 5 needs nothing more. Answer 3 👍: display rules depend only on the display. Answer 4 👎: no glyph–digit table exists, so the earlier "key 1 = 5" press was all the keypad ever needed. Answer 6: [👍 👇 ✌ 🙏] — a properly sealed canonical plan: **cut wire 2, nothing else.** That's the yellow, middle wire — and happily, "middle of three" is the one wire Blind can identify with zero left/right frame, so spatial ambiguity is gone. The wrinkle: Blind sent [✌] — "I now feel changes" — most plausibly just the announced keypad opening, which Mute already knew about when sealing the plan. But timing matters: Mute speaks first each round, so Mute's sealed plan may predate Blind's freshest report. I won't let Blind cut on my word alone; I'll require an explicit thumbs-up from Mute next round as the trigger — Mute hears Blind's speech directly, so Mute can vet the felt changes and veto in their slot before Blind's hand moves.
